summary: Scribble Flow - draw on a blank canvas, SDXL + ControlNet renders it

Open question 2 answered in code: composePaintLayer and the whole output path are already media-independent. Only two display lines depend on the photo (MpiStepPaint.js 588 and 609), so it is a value-source swap not a new component. Silent trap recorded: with no media _natural stays 1x1 and the flow ships a 1x1 PNG with no error. Question 1 narrowed to whether a gizmo step can read a flow-level field at mount.
todo -> doing. Design settled, work starting.

Open question 1 ANSWERED in code, and the answer removes the cross-step dependency entirely. The ratio must be a field on the PAINT STEP ITSELF, not a ratio step and not a flow-level field: a gizmo step's own declared fields seed into _stepValues[role].fields at SETUP (MpiBaseFlow.js:381-393) and that object is handed to the gizmo as props.value at mount, so the ratio is readable before the first _report() with zero frame plumbing; the frame ALSO already calls el.onField(id,val) on a step-field change (MpiBaseFlow.js:1326) with a comment naming 'a ratio lock' as the use case. A flow-level field would NOT be readable - mount props are {media,step,value,onChange} and _fieldValues is not among them. No new field type needed either: declaredFields.js supports select and radio. Zero-media flows already work end to end - character-sheet has no inputSchema and step 0 renders 'This flow needs no input media.' THREE frame/gizmo touch points remain, all small: (1) MpiBaseFlow.js:1284 _buildStepSlide refuses to mount a gizmo when _mediaForRole(role) is null, printing 'Add the image for this step on the first step.'; (2) MpiBaseFlow.js:2211 _deriveRunMedia does 'if (!media) continue', so with nothing uploaded the painted layer never becomes media at all - this is the second half of the same blocker and is easy to miss; (3) MpiStepPaint.js:588 holds ALL init (_natural, paint.init, undo.clear, _syncCanvasSize, _refit, restore, _draw, _report) inside the imgEl load handler, which never fires with no url - extract it to _initSurface(w,h) and call it directly from the ratio. That extraction is exactly what kills the brief's silent 1x1 PNG trap.

Naming DECIDED to kill the collision the brief flagged: user-facing title stays Fabio's 'Scribble', but the internal id is 'blank-canvas' and the op is 'flowBlankCanvas' (gallery prefix FLOWBLANKCANVAS_). Rejected 'scribble'/'flowScribble' - it shares the flowScrib prefix with Draw It In's flowScribObj and reads the same at a glance, which is the exact confusion the brief asked to avoid.

BRIEF PREMISE IS STALE - the SDXL half is ALREADY GONE from HEAD. The brief says to lift flow_draw_it_in.json nodes 17-27, but MPI-621 (249bd357, 'Draw It In is one Klein 9B edit') already landed the Klein rebuild: that file at HEAD is 35 Klein nodes with no ScribblePreprocessor, no CannyEdgePreprocessor, no SetUnionControlNetType, no ControlNetApplyAdvanced, no MpiNormalizeValue and no SDXL loader anywhere. Node 17 at HEAD is PrimitiveStringMultiline Input_Positive and node 26 is MpiInt Input_Seed - the numbers in the brief no longer address the nodes it means. Fabio's 'let's just make sure that we don't lose the SDXL information' has therefore already half-happened, and the ONLY surviving copy is git. RECOVERED from fe525d8e (the commit before the rebuild): 68 nodes, the SDXL render half is 1-35. Saved to scratchpad for this build. Any future session must take the graph from fe525d8e, never from HEAD.

THE REMAP CEILING IS 0.6, NOT THE BRIEF'S 0.5 - and shipping 0.5 would ship the value Fabio measured as broken. The brief says 'MpiNormalizeValue(0-1 -> 0-0.5)'. The recovered graph says output_max 0.6, and flowsRegistry at fe525d8e explains why: 0.5 is the HOUSE number because it is the minimum safe ceiling across every control type an SDXL card offers, and OPENPOSE and DEPTH are what set that floor. Draw It In was allowed to exceed it because its graph hard-wires only two banks (hed/pidi/scribble/ted and canny/lineart/anime_lineart/mlsd) and carries no pose or depth preprocessor at all. Re-swept live 2026-08-23: 0.5 did NOT follow the drawing (Fabio had to force the subject through the prompt, runs 1c5dd5b6 / bbe85266), 0.65 overshot and put the doodle through as edges, 0.6 was his call between them. end_percent stays 0.569, slider stays 0-1. Scribble inherits the same two banks and no pose/depth, so it clears the stated bar and takes 0.6.

TEST GATE FOUND: tests/flow-model-choice.test.cjs 'every ControlNet workflow shares ONE strength mapping' SWEEPS comfy_workflows/*.json and asserts output_max === CEILING[file] ?? 0.5. At HEAD CEILING is {} - MPI-621 emptied it because the only exception's graph was deleted, explicitly 'NOT because the rule was relaxed'. So the new graph at 0.6 FAILS npm test until flow_blank_canvas.json is added to CEILING with the reasoning. The test also asserts end_percent <= 0.6 on every ControlNetApplyAdvanced, which 0.569 satisfies. This is the gate that would otherwise read as 'my new workflow broke an unrelated test'.

GRAPH SHAPE SETTLED (~24 nodes, from the recovered 1-35 plus the LoRA rack). KEEP: 2 Input_Paint, 5 EmptyImage flat white, 3 InvertMask + 6 ImageCompositeMasked (drawing over white = the hint), 8/9 AIO_Preprocessor scribble+canny, 10 Input_Control_Net, 11+16 MpiAnySwitch, 12 CheckpointLoaderSimple Input_Base_Model, 13 ControlNetLoader, 14/15 SetUnionControlNetType, 17 Input_Positive, 19 Input_Negative, 20/21 CLIPTextEncode, 22/23/24 the strength chain, 25 EmptyLatentImage, 26 Input_Seed, 27 KSampler (lcm/simple/7/1.5), 28 VAEDecode, 146 Output_Image, 171-176 Input_Lora_Phase1_*, 170 MpiClearVram. DROP: 1 Input_Image (no photo), 4+7 the bbox crop (Scribble's hint is the WHOLE canvas, not a crop around the drawing), 18 StringConcatenate (the isolate-on-white suffix - brief is explicit that MPI-618 does not apply), 29-35 rembg/scale/stitch, and the entire Klein 100-108/160-169 blend phase. SIZING DECIDED: no Input_Width/Input_Height injection at all. GetImageSize off Input_Paint feeds EmptyImage and EmptyLatentImage, so the ratio arrives implicitly as the PNG's own dimensions - which is exactly what the ratio field seeds _natural to. The ratio select must therefore emit SDXL-native buckets (1024x1024, 1152x896, 896x1152, 1216x832, 832x1216) or the render is off-bucket.

SOURCE GRAPH CHANGED - Fabio prunes the SDXL t2i template, not the recovered Draw It In graph. His read is correct: t2i_sdxl_realistic.json (86 nodes) already carries everything Scribble needs. Input_Control_Net 1624 selects across FOUR arms in order 1=openpose(1620/1576), 2=depth(1602/1625), 3=scribble(1617/1626), 4=canny(1615/1627), switched by MpiAnySwitch 1629 (preprocessor) and 1623 (bank). Strength chain is Input_Control_strength 1622 -> MpiNormalizeValue 1621 (output_max 0.5) -> ControlNetApplyAdvanced 1578 (end_percent 0.569). LoRA rack is Input_Lora_1..6 (1535-1540). Sizing is Input_Width 1633 / Input_Height 1634 -> EmptyLatentImage 1455, so the ratio can inject as params and needs NO GetImageSize off the paint layer - this SUPERSEDES the earlier sizing decision, which was made against the Draw It In graph. Input_Image 1640 is MpiLoadImageFromPath with block_if_empty true, already path-reading and self-gating, and is where the paint layer plugs in.

TRAP - DO NOT PRUNE raw/sdxl_t2i_template.json IN PLACE. Its _template suffix routes it to a GENERATOR, and it is the single source that produces BOTH shipped runtime workflows t2i_sdxl_realistic.json AND t2i_sdxl_nsfw.json. Pruning it would gut the SDXL model cards, not just build the flow. Copy it to a BARE-name raw file (comfy_workflows/raw/flow_blank_canvas.json) first - a bare name routes to a direct runtime file, which is the flow case.

THE CEILING NOW FOLLOWS FROM WHICH ARMS SURVIVE, and this is the argument for pruning to two. Keep all four arms (openpose + depth present) and the house 0.5 stands - no test change, but 0.5 is the exact value Fabio measured on Draw It In as 'did not follow the drawing at all' (runs 1c5dd5b6 / bbe85266), so the flow would ship weak by construction. Prune to scribble + canny only and the graph provably cannot drive openpose or depth, which is the stated bar in flow-model-choice.test.cjs, so it earns the 0.6 he actually shipped. Pruning the two arms is therefore not tidiness - it is what LETS the flow use the strength that works.

TRAP - THE FLAT-WHITE COMPOSITE MUST COME ACROSS FROM THE DRAW IT IN GRAPH; the SDXL template does not have it. In the template the preprocessors read Input_Image 1640 DIRECTLY, because that input is an opaque photo. Scribble's input is the paint gizmo's RGBA layer, whose RGB is undefined wherever alpha is 0 - feed that straight to ScribblePreprocessor and it reads the transparent region as black, so a dark drawing on nothing gives a near-empty or inverted hint. Draw It In solved it with three nodes that must be carried over: EmptyImage (5, colour 16777215 white, sized from the paint layer), InvertMask (3, off the loader's alpha) and ImageCompositeMasked (6, paint over white). Wire 6's output into the preprocessors in place of 1640's direct image link.

LORAS CONFIRMED (Fabio, mid-turn: 'this is gonna have loras') - and the template's rack must be RETITLED, not kept as found. commandExecutor.js _buildParams emits, per declared phase, Lora_Phase<N>_<i> and - for phase 1 ONLY - the flat compatibility key Lora_<i>, both then canonicalized to Input_*. So the SDXL template's existing Input_Lora_1..6 (nodes 1535-1540) WOULD fill correctly for a single-phase flow via that compat line. Keeping it is still wrong: the comment states 'No flow with a declared rack is on that form any more' (character_sheet was the last, phase-titled by MPI-610), the line is documented as currently firing into nothing and marked 'Drop this line once no flow graph has flat nodes', and it warns that a graph carrying BOTH forms takes the same rack TWICE. Shipping Scribble flat would resurrect a compat path the codebase is retiring and make it the only rack-bearing flow on the old form. DECIDED: retitle 1535-1540 to Input_Lora_Phase1_1..6. Verified all five candidate cards (sdxl-realistic, sdxl-nsfw, ill-anime-beauty, ill-anime, pony-mix) are flat-slot with no loraStages, so none trips the 'staged-LoRA model; skipped' bail and the rack works across the whole choosable slot. The rack is the MODEL's own settings, so it follows whichever card the user picked - declare loras: true on the slot, never a flow-level settingsModel.

ANSWER to Fabio 'the original workflow didn't use any negative prompting, did it?' - it had one wired, and it NEVER FIRED. Draw It In node 19 PrimitiveStringMultiline is titled Input_Negative and holds a baked 'blurry, low quality, watermark, text, multiple objects, cropped', wired 19 -> 21 CLIPTextEncode -> 24 ControlNetApplyAdvanced.negative. But commandExecutor.js:611 _buildParams emits `Input_Negative: negative || ''` on EVERY universal run, unconditionally - the exact counterpart of the documented Input_Positive trap - and the FlowDef declared only `positive`, `Input_Control_Net` and `Input_Control_strength` as fields, never a `negative`. So payload.negative was always undefined, the empty string was injected over node 19 on every single run, and the baked negative never reached the sampler. Every Draw It In render ever made ran with an EMPTY negative. Nothing failed and nothing logged; injection matching a real node and writing '' is indistinguishable from success.

PLAYBOOK GAP - the add-flow README documents this trap for Input_Positive only ('A flow with NO prompt must not TITLE its prompt node Input_Positive'), citing Head Swap and Outpaint as leaving the node untitled. The identical hazard on Input_Negative is undocumented, and it bit a shipped flow. The rule generalises: _buildParams emits Input_Positive, Input_Negative and Input_Negative_Audio unconditionally, so ANY of those three titles on a node whose value the flow does not declare as a field is silently wiped. Fix the playbook line to name all three when this card closes.

DECISION for Scribble: KEEP the negative and DECLARE it. Three options were open - expose a `negative` field, bake it and leave the node untitled (the Head Swap / Outpaint dodge), or drop negative prompting entirely. Exposing wins because the base is SDXL: unlike the flow-matching models the newer flows run on, SDXL and especially the Illustrious/Pony arms in this flow's choosable slot respond strongly to a negative, and the SDXL t2i template already has 1473 Input_Negative wired correctly through to the sampler, so keeping it costs nothing and the field is one line. Baking-and-untitling would work but hides a control the model genuinely wants and leaves the flow's five arms sharing one invisible string.

NEGATIVE PROMPT DECIDED BY FABIO 2026-08-26 - BAKED, NOT EXPOSED. This overrides my recommendation to declare a `negative` field; his call, and it is the Head Swap / Outpaint dodge. The string is: blurry, (lowres:1.2), (worst quality:1.4), (low quality:1.4), (bad anatomy:1.4), bad hands, multiple views, jpeg artifacts . Rationale that makes it the better call: the weighted A1111 syntax is expert-tuned per SDXL family and a user text box invites wrecking it, while a bake gives all five arms of the choosable slot one strong correct negative. IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT, and it is the whole point - the node must NOT keep the title Input_Negative. commandExecutor.js:611 emits `Input_Negative: negative || ''` unconditionally, which is exactly why Draw It In's baked negative never fired. Retitle the SDXL template's node 1473 (PrimitiveStringMultiline, currently Input_Negative) to a neutral title - Draw It In used `MpiText | Edit Guardrails` for the same dodge - and set his string as the value. Injection silently skips a title with no node, so the emitted empty string lands nowhere and the bake survives. CLIPTextEncode parses the (term:weight) syntax natively, so no extra node is needed. Consequence for the FlowDef: declare NO `negative` field.

block_if_empty OFF on Input_Image - Fabio's call, and it is correct; my objection was wrong and is retracted. I warned that img.py:396 returns a 1x1 BLACK image with width/height 0, recreating the silent 1x1 trap in the graph. I had missed that the 1x1 goes straight through Scale Image to Total Pixels. Verified in the engine source (comfy_extras/nodes_post_processing.py:247): total = megapixels*1024*1024 = 1048576, scale_by = sqrt(1048576/1) = 1024, and with his resolution_steps 16 the result is round(1*1024/16)*16 = 1024. So an empty path normalises to exactly 1024x1024 on a multiple of 16. GetImageSize reads the SCALED image, so the loader's 0,0 width/height outputs are never consumed. torch.zeros is BLACK, which is the correct neutral for both surviving arms - scribble and canny both encode strokes as white-on-black, so a uniform black hint reads as 'no strokes' and ControlNet contributes nothing. Net behaviour with nothing supplied: a plain 1024x1024 txt2img, which is a better product outcome than an ExecutionBlocker returning no output at all.

CONSEQUENCE - the app-side empty-run guard is CANCELLED, do not build it. I had planned a guard for 'no upload + no drawing + a prompt' because that path would hit block_if_empty and end with no output and no clear reason. With block_if_empty off that case is now a legitimate run that returns a 1024x1024 image, so there is nothing to refuse. promptRequired on the op still covers the genuinely empty case (no prompt AND no image) through the frame's existing guard at MpiBaseFlow _run. One less piece of code.

ALSO RETRACTED EARLIER THE SAME SESSION - the flat-white composite nodes (EmptyImage / InvertMask / ImageCompositeMasked) are NOT needed in the graph. That advice was carried over from Draw It In, which needed them because it had TWO image inputs (photo to Input_Image, RGBA drawing to Input_Paint) and had to flatten the drawing in-graph. Scribble has ONE image input, so the APP composites instead and hands the graph an opaque RGB image. This also makes the optional-upload case free: the app composites strokes over the upload if present and over white if not, and the graph never learns which happened. Fabio's graph as built - Input_Image -> Scale Image to Total Pixels -> the two preprocessors - is already correct with nothing between.

INPUT MEDIA IS OPTIONAL, and canvas creation lives on STAGE 2 (Fabio, 2026-08-26). The user may draw in-app OR upload a drawing made elsewhere (Photoshop), so stage 1 declares ONE image slot, mode 'upto' max 1, labelled Optional. Stage 1 was considered and rejected for the ratio control: it is not that stage 1 lacks selection tooling, it is that _buildInputsSlide has NO declared-widget surface at all - it renders media slots plus the hero/description and never calls _buildField - so putting a control there invents step-0 fields as a new frame concept that every flow then inherits. Stage 2 already has a frame-owned fields row and a gizmo step's fields arrive as props.value.fields AT MOUNT, so the ratio is one declaration and zero frame work. DO NOT crop an uploaded image to the ratio: GetImageSize drives W/H off the supplied image, so the upload's own dimensions are the user's intent, and the ratio governs ONLY the blank-canvas case. The frame has no conditional-field support, so the ratio renders even when an image is present - solve that with COPY ('Canvas size', noting an added image keeps its own size), not by adding a showWhen to the field vocabulary.

PAINT STEP CONTRACT for this flow: role 'image1' with NO mediaRole - the composite REPLACES the upload for that role, which is the semantics `crop` already uses ('a padded picture REPLACES the picture it was padded from'), not the `paint` semantics Draw It In used. MpiStepPaint must therefore export the COMPOSITE, not composePaintLayer's layer-alone: _draw() at MpiStepPaint.js:294-302 already renders image-then-layer on screen, so this is a second export path beside the existing one rather than new machinery. The two MpiBaseFlow blockers still stand and both fire on the no-upload path: _buildStepSlide's media guard (1284) and _deriveRunMedia's `if (!media) continue` (2211).

PROVEN LIVE on the bench by Fabio 2026-08-26: with no image AND no prompt the graph completes and returns a clean portrait, Output_Image reporting 1024 x 1024. That confirms the whole traced chain empirically rather than by reading alone - MpiLoadImageFromPath with block_if_empty off emits a 1x1 black tensor, Scale Image to Total Pixels normalises it to exactly 1024x1024, both preprocessors read uniform black as 'no strokes' so ControlNet contributes nothing, and what remains is a plain SDXL txt2img on an empty prompt. Fabio's words: 'it creates whatever the model will create without the prompt.' The empty-path fallback is therefore SAFE and needs no app-side guard - this closes the question rather than leaving it as a traced prediction.

OPEN PRODUCT CALL raised by that test: declare promptRequired on flowBlankCanvas? 'It does not crash' is not 'it is what the user wanted' - an empty prompt returns an arbitrary portrait, which is a confusing result to hand someone who just hit Generate. Draw It In's op already declares promptRequired for the SAME reason (an empty prompt there produced 'a shape invented from the ControlNet hint alone', which Fabio hit and MPI-606 bug 5 then made the frame actually honour at MpiBaseFlow _run). Both of this flow's empty cases are covered by it: no drawing + no prompt gives the random portrait above, and drawing + no prompt gives a subject invented from the hint. RECOMMEND promptRequired: true, pending Fabio's call.

NEW FRAME CAPABILITY - a paint step can now run with NO source media, and it took three edits plus one new declaration. (1) MpiStepPaint: extracted _initSurface(w,h) out of the imgEl load handler, which is what previously held ALL init, so a media-less mount ran none of it and reported 1x1; added _blankSize() reading the step's own canvasSize field from props.value at mount; _draw now paints a white ground when there is no source instead of drawImage on a never-loaded Image; added el.onField to re-arm on a size change. (2) stepKinds: STEP_MEDIA now receives the STEP, and paint branches on step.composite between composePaintLayer (layer alone, Draw It In) and the new composePaintComposite (flattened over source-or-white, Scribble). Declared rather than inferred from mediaRole on purpose - the correlation holds for two flows and is not a rule. (3) MpiBaseFlow: both blockers lifted behind `&& !step.composite` - the _buildStepSlide mount guard and _deriveRunMedia's `if (!media) continue` - plus media?.mediaType on the appended item, which would have thrown on the null-source path. ponytail ceiling recorded in code: el.onField refuses a resize once anything is drawn, because re-arming calls undo.clear() and an unconditional resize would destroy a drawing with no way back; upgrade to a real rescale only if someone asks to change shape mid-drawing.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED - the canvas-size picker moved but the canvas stayed square, and it was MY bug. el.onField called _blankSize(), which re-reads props.value?.fields?.canvasSize. props.value is the object captured in the closure AT MOUNT, and the frame writes a field by REPLACING the step's value object (_writeDeclaredField: _stepValues[role] = { ...prev, fields: {...} }), so the captured object keeps the ORIGINAL size forever. The control moved, nothing else did, and nothing errored. FIX: take the new value from the argument the frame already passes - el.onField(fieldId, val) - and parse THAT. Split _parseSize(raw) out so mount-time (_blankSize off props.value, correct there) and change-time (off val) share one parser. Generalises: a gizmo must never re-read props.value to learn about a change, because the frame hands it a new object rather than mutating the old one.

UI REWORK from Fabio's first live look at the step (2026-08-26), four issues, all four fixed. (1) CANVAS TOO SMALL to draw a whole figure. (2) The size picker and prompt should sit LEFT of the canvas. (3) The size control's placement 'is just bad - not centred in the text box, floating and not coherent'. (4) Dropdown options truncated to 'Squa...', 'Port...', 'Land...'. 1-3 are one change: a new OPT-IN step flag `fieldsSide` puts the step's declared fields in a stacked 300px column BESIDE the canvas instead of under it, freeing the vertical the drawing wants and dissolving the alignment complaint (labels sit above their controls in the stacked form). Opt-in rather than the new default because _buildStepSlide is the frame EVERY gizmo step in every flow renders through and three shipped steps are laid out for the stacked form. CSS: --split raises the work cap to 1320px, the fields column is flex 0 0 300px so the canvas takes every remaining pixel, and the paint stage is SIZED up to min(68vh, 760px) from its stacked min(46vh, 500px) - sizing a hosted gizmo, which a consumer block is allowed to do; no chrome is restated.

DROPDOWN TRUNCATION ROOT CAUSE, and it is a Primitive bug that predates this flow: MpiDropdown.js positionList() did `list.style.width = rect.width + 'px'`, pinning the portalled menu to the TRIGGER's width. A trigger narrower than its own longest option therefore ellipsised every option (.mpi-dropdown__option gets text-overflow: ellipsis), so the user picked between 'Squa...' and 'Land...'. FIX: the trigger width becomes a FLOOR - minWidth = rect.width with width: max-content - plus a max-width: min(420px, 100vw - 16px) in the stylesheet so a long option cannot open a window-wide menu, plus an overhang correction on `left` so a right-hand control no longer opens past the viewport edge now that the menu may exceed its trigger. Swept as a shared primitive: this only ever REVEALS text that was hidden, never narrows a menu, and the desktop specs that exercise MpiDropdown (model-settings-popup, popup-contract) stay green.

THE RESHAPE NOW CARRIES THE DRAWING - the refuse-when-drawn guard is REMOVED, and Fabio's reaction is why. He said he had not tested changing the canvas size because he was 'afraid I might lose my beautiful drawing'. The drawing was in fact safe (el.onField bailed on !paint.isEmpty()), but a control that moves and does nothing is worse than either real behaviour: he would not touch it at all rather than risk a picture he had just spent real time on. Fixed properly instead of documented: on a size change the layer is CONTAIN-FIT into the new canvas and restored. New helper _refitLayer(url, from, to) pre-renders into the destination size, and that pre-render is load-bearing rather than tidy - PaintManager.setFromDataURL does drawImage(img, 0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height), so handing it a square layer for a wide canvas would STRETCH the drawing rather than place it. Contain, centred, never crop: the user drew a whole picture and changing the page shape must not decide which part to discard. _initSurface(w, h, restoreUrl = seeded.paint) now takes what to restore, so mount-time seeding and reshape-time carrying share one path.

SECOND BUG FIXED IN THE SAME EDIT, and it would have silently distorted every reshaped drawing. _layerUrl() memoises the exported PNG behind _urlDirty and only 'the four real mutations' set that flag - a reshape was not one of them. So after a resize the memo still held the layer at the OLD size while _natural reported the NEW one, and composePaintComposite draws the layer across the full w x h: a square layer stretched into a wide frame, no error, no warning. _initSurface now sets _urlDirty = true unconditionally. Cost is one extra encode at mount. PROVEN by the layer coming back at 1344x768 after the reshape rather than the stale 1024x1024.

VERIFIED - the carry is proven at the pixel level through the REUSE path rather than by drawing, because synthetic PointerEvents never reach the brush (pointer capture rejects an untrusted event; both the stage and the canvas element were tried and getValue().paint stayed empty). A stretch would have read ~197x112. That single measurement covers _refitLayer, the restoreUrl parameter and the _urlDirty fix at once. ponytail ceiling recorded in the code: the reshape itself is not undoable, because undo.clear() is part of arming a surface. Reaching for a size and reaching back costs one contain-fit round trip, so square -> wide -> square leaves the drawing smaller than it started. Record the reshape as a real undo entry if anyone bounces between shapes often enough to notice.

CONTAIN-FIT ON RESHAPE WAS WRONG AND IS REPLACED BY A 1:1 RE-CANVAS. Fabio hit it on his SECOND reshape: square -> portrait gave white spacing on top, portrait -> square came back with the drawing visibly smaller and margin on all four sides, and he called it - 'it's most likely going to keep adding spacing if we go down that route'. Correct: each reshape contain-fit the ALREADY-FITTED result, so the drawing shrank and gained margin every single time. I had written that up as an accepted ponytail ceiling ('square -> wide -> square leaves the drawing smaller than it started'); hitting it on the second interaction means it was never an acceptable ceiling, it was a bug. The deeper error was scaling at all. The control is called CANVAS SIZE, so it changes the PAGE the drawing sits on - exactly what an image editor's canvas-size command does - and never resizes the artwork. _refitLayer is now _recanvasLayer: draw at 1:1, centred, transparent where the page grew, cropped where it shrank. Simpler than the scaling version too (no scale maths).

THE MASTER LAYER is what makes the round trip lossless, and without it the re-canvas would erode the drawing just as badly in the other direction. Re-canvassing CROPS whichever axis shrank, so feeding the next reshape the cropped result would lose those pixels permanently. New `_master` holds the layer as last DRAWN, never as last reshaped, and every re-canvas works from it. Refreshed only when the user has actually drawn since it was taken, detected via `_urlDirty` - which is a valid signal precisely because _report() clears that flag at the end of every reshape, so a true reading means real strokes rather than the reshape's own re-encode. Seeded lazily, so the reuse path (mount with value.paint, then reshape) is covered by the same branch.

PROVEN LOSSLESS with pixel measurements on the seeded-layer path. Baseline: a 200x200 mark at (100,100) in a 1024x1024 layer reads bbox [100,100,298,298], 198x198 at the 2px sampling step. SQUARE -> PORTRAIT (896x1152): bbox [36,164,234,362], mark still 198x198 - matching the hand-computed 1:1 centred offsets exactly (x -64, y +64) and confirming no scaling. PORTRAIT -> SQUARE: bbox [100,100,298,298], 198x198 - IDENTICAL to baseline. Then a five-reshape chain 1344x768 -> 768x1344 -> 1152x896 -> 896x1152 -> 1024x1024 returned [100,100,298,298] with lossless true. The 1344x768 step reads 198x170 because the mark's top 28px goes off-canvas - the crop a canvas resize SHOULD do - and it returns to 198x198 on the next reshape, which is the master proving the crop is display-only and not destructive. npm test 738/738 after the change.

THE SKIPPED STEP WAS A SPARSE-ARRAY HOLE, and the root is one character. `_mediaGroups[].items` is SPARSE BY CONTRACT - clearing a slot `delete`s its index rather than splicing, so later images keep the role their slot names, and the code says so ('a hole means that slot is empty, which is legal'). But `Array.prototype.find` is one of the few iterators that does NOT skip holes: it calls back with `undefined`. `_mediaForRole` used a bare `it.role`, so the first navigation after clearing a filled slot threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'role')`. Fixed to `it?.role`. The `delete` is CORRECT and was left alone - splicing would silently shift every later image into another slot's role, which is a worse bug than the one being fixed. Swept every other reader of `items` in the file: line 828 uses index access (a hole reads undefined, falsy, fine), 2099 uses `.filter(Boolean)` (filter skips holes), 736/851 are direct writes. 558 was the only hole-intolerant one.

WHY THIS BUG WAS INVISIBLE IN EVERY CHANNEL THAT NORMALLY CATCHES ONE, worth keeping because the symptom pointed at the wrong subsystem for four wrong hypotheses. The TypeError fired inside `_renderSlide` BEFORE `slidesEl.innerHTML = ''`, so the DOM never swapped while `_current` had ALREADY been advanced by `_goTo`. Result: press Next once and nothing appears to happen; press again and it lands on Generate, which builds no gizmo and never calls `_mediaForRole`. It reads exactly like 'the flow skips the middle step', which is how Fabio reported it, and it sent me looking at `_getSteps`, `_syncChrome`, `_lastIndex` and `STEP_KINDS` - all of which are static and all of which were fine. It was an UNCAUGHT renderer TypeError, so nothing reached `clientLogger` and app.log showed a clean session; and the node suite cannot reach it because the bug only exists once a slot has really been filled and then cleared. What finally found it was reproducing in an isolated instance and reading the CONSOLE, not the log. Fabio's own detail - 'first press stays, second takes me to the last stage' - is the signature of a throw between the index write and the DOM swap; treat that shape as diagnostic.

SECOND BUG IN THE SAME HANDLER: clearing a slot THREW AWAY THE USER'S TYPED PROMPT. `delete _stepValues[freedRole]` was justified as 'a removed image invalidates the step bound to that role', which is right about the DRAWING - those strokes were placed over the image that just left - and wrong about everything else in that record. A gizmo step's DECLARED FIELD VALUES live in `_stepValues[role].fields`, and for Scribble that is both `canvasSize` AND `positive`, the user's own words. So removing an upload silently discarded a typed prompt and reset the canvas size to Square. Now the record is rebuilt as `{ fields }` - the paint layer and brush state go, the declared fields stay. Found by reading, not reported: Fabio only noticed the canvas-size half.

PROVEN BY REPRODUCTION, BEFORE AND AFTER, in an isolated instance (own port 60689, own profile) rather than by argument. BEFORE: seed a filled slot, click clear, press Next - console carries `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'role')` with the full stack `_mediaForRole:558 -> _buildStepSlide:1284 -> _renderSlide:1492 -> _goTo:1511`, and the ticker stays on index 0. AFTER: start 0, clear, still 0, Next -> index 1 WITH a mounted canvas (so it is the real gizmo, not the 'add an image' placeholder), Next -> index 2, and zero console errors. New regression spec tests/desktop/flow-clear-slot-advances.spec.js drives that exact sequence and asserts the middle index plus an empty console - a node test cannot see this, and no log line exists to assert on. Suites: npm test 737/738 (the one failure is the unrelated orphan-sweep isolation leak), npm run test:desktop 27/27, eslint clean. No mutation test was run to prove the spec fails without the fix: the pre-fix stack trace is that evidence already, and a mutation run that dies mid-way leaves a real source file broken on disk.

STILL OPEN AND IT IS A UX CALL, NOT A BUG: the canvas-size picker is inert when an image is uploaded. `_hasMedia` is a `const` captured at mount and `onField` bails on it (`if (fieldId !== 'canvasSize' || _hasMedia) return`). That is BY DESIGN - the FlowDef predicted it in a comment ('it renders even when the user HAS uploaded a drawing, because the frame has no conditional-field support ... answered with copy rather than a showWhen, a real feature with real blast radius for one control'). Fabio hit it and reported it, which is the same shape as the reshape guard he rejected earlier: 'a control that moves and does nothing is worse than either real behaviour'. Three ways out, and it is his pick: hide the field when a slot is filled (needs `showWhen` in the field vocabulary), disable it with a reason on the control, or make it WORK by re-canvassing the uploaded image the same 1:1 centred way `_recanvasLayer` already re-canvasses the paint layer - which is coherent with the semantic already settled here, that canvas size changes the PAGE and never the artwork. NOT actioned without his call.

CANVAS SIZE IS NOW DISABLED WHEN THE SLOT IS FILLED - Fabio picked option 2 of three (hide / disable / make it work). New STEP-FIELD flag `blankOnly: true`, resolved in `_buildFieldsRow` against `_mediaForRole(step.role)` and passed down as `disabled`. Chosen over a general `showWhen` predicate deliberately: one boolean with one meaning, against a expression language the frame would then own forever for a single control. The FlowDef's old note ('Only used for a blank canvas') was fine print under a live control; reworded to 'Sets the size of a blank canvas. REUSE MUST NEVER COST THE USER THEIR DRAWING - Fabio, 2026-08-26, and it reverses the current behaviour in `flowService.openFlowFromReuse`. Today a flow whose models are not installed is REFUSED: `flowAvailability()` fails, the user gets 'needs its model installed - opening Flows' and is redirected to the Flow Library, so the flow never opens and the saved `flowInputs` - which for Scribble is the DRAWING - are never restored. Surface it as a TOAST rather than a redirect: a warning when a different candidate will run, and an ERROR toast roughly 'No models installed for this flow' when NO candidate of a slot is installed - still with the flow open and the drawing intact, so the user can install and press Generate rather than rebuild their picture.
